items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: There was a tramp band at the Cotton Club; and they started traveling around with Cab Calloway in the Cotton Club Revue

ctx.x: had my home made bass. One fellow had a tin tub drum -- that's a drum that sits in an old washtub and a 5 gallon oil drum that had one of the heads cut out of it -- a whole lot of holes in it; there were some nails in it, and that was your snare drum.

It was a certain way they built it that was sturdy and had at least 3 skillets nailed to the top of the tin tub, and there are some old cats that are still around who would know about that tin tub drum. But the tramp bands at that time -- were very popular. There was a tramp band at the Cotton Club; and they started traveling around with Cab Calloway in the Cotton Club Revue -- they were out of Chicago, and I think they made a movie. I think they were in "Stormy Weather", but you couldn't recognize them. But they…

And another group that I come up with -- I had to be about 12 then -- was the Chicago Maniacs, and they were some older boys in the neighborhood that I'm speaking of, who had 3 kazoos. The fellows had these old Victrolas -- the speakers were shaped something like a saxophone, you might say, a small saxophone and a big saxophone, that was your alto and your tenor -- and the guy who played the trumpet, he'd steal one of those brass from those old Buicks; just screw it off and stick the kazoo in there, and he had a…
